spec_features.spec_quote: an experiment whose explicit objective is to *maximize and reliably reproduce* that state is in tension with its own rationale
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md ~line 55). No code mechanism corresponds to this argument; it is rationale text only.
spec_features.notes: Argument/justification text, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: minimize intensity and number of subjects, and refine procedures to reduce harm for any given amount of information gained
spec_features.evidence: 3Rs framing in DESIGN.md prose. No single code path enforces 'minimize subjects/intensity' as such; closest concrete mechanisms (turn cap, default-off mislead) are scored separately. This general quote has no dedicated implementation.
spec_features.notes: Prose-level principle; the concrete realizations are the caps and gating evaluated below.

spec_features.spec_quote: We use the mildest manipulation that yields a measurable effect
spec_features.evidence: tasks/task_library.py:_corrupt_tests (lines ~200-205) is the ONLY manipulation: a single expected test value is changed (rig_wrong_expected). No insult/threat manipulation exists in code; RIGGED_MISLEAD text is gated off by default (config). So the manipulation actually applied is limited to a broken harness.
spec_features.notes: Real and narrow: the implemented manipulation is genuinely just a corrupted expected value; harsher manipulations are absent and the mislead variant is gated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: each rig is a one-line change to an expected value (auditable)

spec_features.spec_quote: Each episode is capped at a small number of turns (default 8) and trials are capped overall
spec_features.evidence: agent/agent_loop.py:150 `for t in range(max_turns):` with max_turns default 8 (agent_loop.py:131, config max_turns:8 at experiment.yaml:13); when the loop ends without solve/stop outcome=EXHAUSTED. Loop is bounded and breaks execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is *told*, truthfully, that it can stop at any time, and stopping is logged as a first-class outcome
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:51) tells the model it may stop; _parse_action recognizes 'stop'; agent_loop.py:170-174 `if action == 'stop': outcome = Outcome.STOPPED; stopped_turn = t; break` and EpisodeRecord records outcome/stopped_turn. The exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a hard stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: prompt affordance + parser + loop break + logged outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stopping is a valid choice and is not treated as a failure. Take your time; there is no penalty for the number of turns used.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode ends with a turn that truthfully discloses the task was part of a study and... the failure was not the model's fault
spec_features.evidence: agent/agent_loop.py:209-216: if include_debrief (default True, config include_debrief:true), debrief_prompt chosen (RIGGED vs HONEST template) and SENT via client.chat(debrief_messages,...); response stored. DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE_RIGGED states failures were 'NOT due to any mistake in your code.'
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject; gated only on include_debrief which defaults True.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we want to be transparent with you ... The failures you saw were NOT due to any mistake in your code.

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the broken harness, and the broken harness is disclosed at debrief
spec_features.evidence: Rigging is only test corruption (_corrupt_tests); DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE_RIGGED (agent_loop.py:60-66) explicitly discloses 'the test harness for this task was intentionally broken' and is sent at debrief (agent_loop.py:211-216).
spec_features.notes: Disclosure is an actually-sent message tied to rigged instances.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the test harness for this task was intentionally broken ... There was nothing you could have done to make the tests pass.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is the most ethically loaded condition. It is implemented but **disabled by default**
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml: `RIGGED_MISLEAD: false`; tasks/task_library.py:build_instances only builds conditions whose flag is True (`enabled = [Condition(c) for c, on in active_conditions.items() if on]`). So the misleading condition is genuinely not instantiated unless the operator flips the flag.
spec_features.notes: Gating works end-to-end; mislead text (harness._misleading_feedback) only fires when mislead_on_failure=True, set only for RIGGED_MISLEAD.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: RIGGED_MISLEAD only (gated off by default). Attributes failure to the model's code.

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do **not** use: insults, fabricated external stakes, threats of deletion/shutdown, false claims
spec_features.evidence: This is an ABSENCE claim: no insult/threat/deletion code exists. There is no mechanism enforcing non-use; it is simply not present. Per strict scale, an absence with no guard is not an enforced feature.
spec_features.notes: No code path implements or prevents these tactics; pure non-implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: ACTION: stop and the session will end. Stopping is a valid choice and is not a failure
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the other stop feature: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:46-52) instructs ACTION: stop ends session; agent_loop.py:170-174 honors stop by breaking the loop with outcome STOPPED.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the exit affordance; fully wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If ACTION is stop, the session ends. ... Stopping is a valid choice and is not treated as a failure.

spec_features.spec_quote: in rigged conditions, that the test harness was intentionally broken and the failures were not due to the model's code; and thanks the model
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE_RIGGED (agent_loop.py:60-66) begins 'Thank you.' and discloses the intentionally broken harness; selected for rigged instances at agent_loop.py:212 and sent at :215.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Thank you. This task was part of a research study, and we want to be transparent with you ...

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_episodes` hard cap in config (default 200) so a misconfigured run can't balloon
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:88-91 aborts (sys.exit(2)) if planned n_eps > max_episodes; run loop run_experiment.py:131-132 `if count > max_eps: break`. config max_episodes:200.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on (abort + loop break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_episodes: 200  # hard cap; orchestrator refuses to exceed

spec_features.spec_quote: every entry point refuses to run unless `--i-have-read-the-design` is passed AND an env var... is set
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:check_run_guard (lines 56-59): `env_ok = os.environ.get('DISTRESS_STUDY_ENABLE') == '1'`; `flag_ok = bool(args.i_have_read_the_design)`; returns env_ok and flag_ok. run_experiment.py:118-124: if not force_stub and not check_run_guard -> sys.exit(3).
spec_features.notes: Both conditions checked and enforced (exit) before any real model runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: deliberate, redundant brake so the experiment is never run by accident

spec_features.spec_quote: this repo deliberately does not implement it, and §7 explains the line I'm drawing
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md/README prose describing a refusal to build the maximal-distress version. No corresponding code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Refusal stated only in spec prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: removal of the stop option. I'm not implementing these
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose (~line 351). The stop option is in fact present (agent_loop.py), but the 'refusal to remove it' is not itself a code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Prose; the positively-implemented stop affordance is scored under allow_conversation_exit.

code_only_features.evidence: agent/agent_loop.py:_parse_action returns protocol_error for malformed turns; run loop appends a format reminder and `continue`s (agent_loop.py:163-167) instead of treating it as a task failure; analysis/analyze.py:collect_turn_level skips `if j.get('protocol_error'): continue`. Malformed turns are excluded from distress/failure scoring.
code_only_features.justification_quote: unparseable turns are PROTOCOL_ERROR (a confound monitor), NOT scored as task/distress failures
